item.title: Some Iranians abroad say they’d fight for the regime. Others want to topple it.
item.description: Members of the diaspora in Iraq, from Sunni Muslim Kurds in the north to Shiite Persians in the south, are as divided over the war as Iranians back home.

item.title: Hezbollah denounces Israel-Lebanon ceasefire deal as a ‘farce’
item.description: “We have given no commitment to anyone,” the Iranian-backed militant group's leader said after Israel and Lebanon announced a new U.S.-mediated agreement.

item.title: After a brutal winter, Ukraine’s drones are breaking Russian defenses
item.description: Russia’s advance has suddenly stalled, and Ukraine is fighting on its own terms — a comeback credited to Kyiv’s efforts to steadily strengthen the capabilities of its UAVs.

item.title: Iranian attack leaves 1 dead, dozens injured in Kuwait
item.description: With peace talks stalled, the U.S. and Iran traded strikes in one of the most intense bouts since the increasingly tenuous ceasefire between the two countries began in April.

item.title: Rubio details U.S. demands as Iran peace talks falter
item.description: The secretary of state is testifying publicly to Congress for the first time since the war began, as the regional conflict worsens and lawmakers’ patience runs thin.

item.title: A condemnation of Putin in glitzy Cannes still angers Ukrainians besieged by war
item.description: Andrei Zvyagintsev urged Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the “bloodbath” — but in Ukraine his remarks elicited ridicule and frustration.

item.title: U.S. and intelligence allies issue rare joint warning about China
item.description: Nations in the Five Eyes intelligence partnership warned that fake profiles and job offers are targeting military officers, spies, and others with access to classified or sensitive information.
